target.name: R Draconis
target.summary_plain: An old, swollen red giant that pulsates, swelling and shrinking over about 246 days. Near the north ecliptic pole, where SPHEREx looks almost every day, so its rhythm shows up as a real light curve.

render.note: One asinh stretch per detector (0.5-99.7 percentiles of all its epochs), shared by every epoch, so brightness changes between frames are real. Co-adds: IMAGE minus ZODI, official photometry mask 0x3C028E44 rejected, OVERFLOW kept and flagged, then an inverse-variance mean after 3-sigma clipping (drops single-exposure streaks). Then vs Now: each image stretched by its own 0.5-99.7 percentiles. Differences: S/N, linear between the limits.

motion.method: Per-exposure ePSF position fits (D1-D6, S/N >= 10, 100 mas floor); sigma-clipped linear fit with parallax removed
motion.verdict_text: R Dra barely moves (22 mas per year in Gaia DR3). The apparent 0.9 ± 0.2″ per year from saturated-core positions (χ²/dof 29) is an artefact of saturation, not motion: R Dra is here for its brightness changes.

notes: Each point is one exposure: forced photometry at the catalogue position (ePSF fit, or a fit to the PSF wings when the core is saturated).
Saturated points are shown hollow and excluded from fits.
842 of 842 points are saturated (OVERFLOW in the core).
The quick-look curve is the Year-1 spectral cube at 12.9″ pixels: it blends close neighbours, and channels where the star saturates are left empty.

warnings: Saturated (OVERFLOW) in 842 of 842 exposures. Saturated pixels are kept in the images and outlined in the flags overlay; their brightness comes from fits to the PSF wings.
Too bright for SPHEREx: the core saturates in every exposure, so brightness comes from the PSF wings and the light curve is relative.
Positions from saturated cores are biased (apparent 0.9″/yr, χ²/dof 29); R Dra's real motion is 0.02″/yr.
6 of 17 epochs are partial (fewer than 12 images per detector): shown greyed out.
False colour exists for 1 of 12 epochs: it needs D1, D3 and D6 in the same epoch, and the deep-field visits sample one detector pair at a time.
Blink frames show 12 of the 17 epochs (those with the most exposures, at most 16 exposures per detector each); the light curve and spectrum use all of them.
